# VDSL Schema Reference (0.1 / 0.2)

Authoritative implementation: `packages/vdsl/src/schema.ts` (zod, strict —
unknown keys are rejected everywhere). Validation errors carry YAML line
numbers. All durations are SECONDS; the compiler converts to frames with
`Math.round(duration × fps)`.

## Storyboard

```yaml
schema_version: "0.2" # defaults to 0.2 when omitted; 0.1 still validates
project:
  id: my-video
  language: zh-CN # zh-CN | en-US
  fps: 30
  width: 1920
  height: 1080
style:
  # next line's theme list is generated by `pnpm run docs:commands` — do not edit
  theme: paper-light # paper-light (default) | dark-tech | ocean-deep | dusk-warm | forest-moss | sunset-pop | terminal-vintage | paper-cream | ai-red
  #                       packages/video-components/src/theme.ts)
defaults: # 0.2, optional project-level defaults
  renderer: remotion # scenes that omit visual.renderer inherit this
assets: # 0.2, optional project-level manifest
  - id: asset-logo
    type: svg # svg|png|jpg|webp|canvas|audio|video|font
    source: generated # generated|user|external
    path: assets/svg/logo.svg
scenes:
  - id: scene-01
    duration: 8
    narration:
      text: "……"
      audio: assets/audio/scene-01.wav # optional; mounted by video audio flows
    visual:
      component: FlowChart
      renderer: remotion # remotion (default) | canvas
      props: { … } # validated against the REGISTRY props schema
    animation: # legacy v0.1 entrance model (still honored)
      entrance: fade # none|fade|slide|scale|draw|typewriter (+synonyms)
      emphasis: none
      exit: none
    animations: # 0.2 timeline model (plan §10), scene-relative
      - id: draw-arrow
        target: arrow-1
        type: draw # draw|write|fade|move|scale|rotate|highlight|morph
        start: 1.2
        duration: 0.8
        easing: easeInOut # linear|easeIn|easeOut|easeInOut (+synonyms)
    captions:
      source: narration # narration|none (+synonyms); text overrides
    transition:
      in: fade # fade|cut (+synonyms); default fade
      out: fade
```

## Themes (`style.theme`)

The palette is chosen per storyboard and resolved by the renderer
(`resolveTheme` in `packages/video-components/src/theme.ts`); unknown or
missing names fall back to `paper-light` (the v0.4.3 default), so a
typo never crashes a render. Pre-v0.4.3 storyboards defaulted to
`dark-tech`; existing 0.1/0.2/0.4.2 storyboards stay valid — set
`theme: dark-tech` explicitly to keep the old look.

| name                                  | background            | ink/text        | accent                  | mood                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------- | --------------- | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `paper-light` (v0.4.3 default)        | `#F5F1E8` warm paper  | `#1F1D1A` ink   | `#C2410C` amber-red     | bright board; pairs with canvas hand-drawn scenes and tutorial content |
| `dark-tech` (default prior to v0.4.3) | `#0B1220` deep navy   | `#E6EDF3`       | `#4C8DFF` blue          | the original technical look; best for dev/protocol topics              |
| `ocean-deep`                          | `#071A1E` deep teal   | `#D9F2EF`       | `#2DD4BF` teal          | calm, softer contrast; monitoring/infra topics                         |
| `dusk-warm`                           | `#1E1420` plum        | `#F5E9E0` cream | `#F97362` coral         | warm, story-led and brand pieces                                       |
| `ai-red`                              | `#0F0F0F` player dark | `#FFFFFF`       | `#FF0000` signature red | creator/playback feel; pairs with the `channel-banner` intro gradient  |

Notes: `DoodleScene`'s `background: paper` always uses its own light
paper regardless of theme (ink-on-paper is the look), so light themes are
safe alongside canvas scenes. The burned-in captions, node fills
and arrows all follow the resolved theme.
Adding a theme = one new entry in the `THEMES` registry (full token set
validated by `isValidTheme` — see `theme.ts` for the contrast rules).

## The `visual` block — what the audience sees

`visual` pairs two choices: `component` (the registered implementation,
validated against `REGISTRY`) and `renderer` (the scene family that draws
it). Current pairings:

| renderer     | component(s)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | look                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `remotion`   | Title, Paragraph, CodeBlock, Terminal, FlowChart, Timeline, Callout, EndCard, Character, Image, ImageBackground, AnimatedIllustration + v0.4.2: QuoteBlock, StatGrid (count-up), BarChart, Leaderboard, Checklist, BigIdea, PyramidDiagram, VennDiagram, CycleDiagram | classic motion graphics on the theme background                                                                                                                     |
| `canvas`     | `DoodleScene`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | hand-drawn ink: procedural strokes (circle / star / zigzag / spiral) with seeded wobble, sequential pen-draw, optional `bpm` beat-sync, `background: paper \| dark` |

`props` are validated against the component's own registry schema, so each
component documents its own shape — `FlowChart` wants `nodes[]` (strings)
and optional `edges[]` ([from, to] index pairs) plus `direction`;
`Title` wants `text` + optional `subtext`. Synonyms are coerced for
`renderer` before validation (`hand-drawn`/`doodle` → `canvas`); unknown
values fail loudly at render time rather than silently substituting a
different look.

The scene family also decides the animation fallback: `canvas` scenes
auto-draw sequentially (strokes, ease-out, ~0.25 s stagger) so a minimal
storyboard still animates; `remotion` components fall back to their
`animation.entrance` model.

## The `animations[]` timeline — the scene's choreography

Scene-relative SECONDS. Each entry animates ONE named element (`target`)
with one verb (`type`) between `start` and `start + duration` (must fit
inside the scene), eased by `easing` (`linear` / `easeIn` / `easeOut` /
`easeInOut`, synonyms like `ease-in-out` accepted).

What each `type` does per scene family:

| type                        | canvas (`DoodleScene`)         | remotion          |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------ | ----------------- |
| `draw`                      | pen strokes draw progressively | wipe-style reveal |
| `write`                     | —                              | typewriter reveal |
| `fade`                      | opacity fade-in                | opacity fade-in   |
| `move` / `scale` / `rotate` | reserved                       | reserved          |
| `highlight`                 | —                              | —                 |
| `morph`                     | reserved                       | reserved          |

`target` refers to an element id inside the scene's props (DoodleScene
stroke id). Elements with no explicit entry use the family's sequential auto-draw
default, so choreography is additive: declare only the beats you care
about (e.g. one arrow draw + one highlight) and let the rest flow.

Timing guidance (from the `animation-principles` skill, encoded in
`@video/motion/src/heuristics.ts`): entrances 0.3–0.8 s ease-out, group
stagger 40–80 ms capped at ~0.7 s total, entrances ≤ ⅓ of the scene, one
highlight beat for scenes ≥ 6 s, key moments on the beat grid when a BPM
is given.

## Rules the validator enforces

- Component must be registered (`REGISTRY`), props must pass its schema.
- Narration audio file must exist and not exceed scene duration
  (tolerance 0.05 s) — run `video preview`/`video make` first: they sync
  durations to measured audio before validating.
- Captions must wrap to ≤ 3 lines of 24 CJK units (bottom safe area).
- Timeline animations must fit inside the scene (`start + duration ≤
duration`).
- LLM synonym coercion is applied BEFORE validation (e.g. `wipe` → `draw`,
  `hand-drawn` → `canvas`, `dissolve` → `fade`); truly unknown values fail
  loudly.

## Renderer inheritance (defaults.renderer)

A scene's `visual.renderer` is optional: an omitted value inherits from
the project-level `defaults.renderer`, falling back to `remotion`.
Precedence: **scene > defaults > remotion**. Inheritance resolves at
parse time — the compiled `vdsl/vdsl.yaml` and the RenderPlan always
carry explicit per-scene renderers (determinism preserved). Strict by
design: an inherited renderer that doesn't fit a scene's component
(e.g. `canvas` + `Title`) still fails loudly at render time
(`assertPlanRenderable`); there is no silent family-aware fallback.

In the article-driven (`video make`) flow, the default is set from
`article.md` frontmatter:

```yaml
---
project: my-video
language: zh-CN
duration_target_sec: 60
voice: zh-CN-YunjianNeural
default_renderer: canvas # → storyboard emits defaults: {renderer: canvas}
---
```

The derived storyboard then carries `schema_version: "0.2"` and the
`defaults:` block. Synonyms work here too (`hand-drawn` → `canvas`).

### `setting:` — era, region, culture (v0.10)

For any historical, period-specific or cultural topic, declare the setting in
`article.md` frontmatter. It is spliced into every scene image brief, where the
expander must state **era + region**, **people's appearance**, and **period
dress/armour/materials** — and rule out the anachronism (plate armour, cathedral,
Renaissance clothing) explicitly.

```yaml
---
project: xuanwumen
image_style: editorial
setting: Tang-dynasty China, 626-630 CE, Tang court and military dress
---
```

Without it the expander infers the era from the scene narration, which is
unreliable: a probe on a `visual:` line with no dynasty marker produced
**"late Ming dynasty, 1620"** for a Tang scene. The key is also part of the
image-brief cache identity, so changing it invalidates briefs written under the
old setting.

`video draft` preserves this key (and `image_style` / `image_provider`) across
re-drafts; `project`, `language`, `duration_target_sec` and `voice` always
reflect the newest run.

### `tts_provider:` — narration backend (voicebox / minimax, v0.9.x)

`video make` can narrate through a local [Voicebox](https://voicebox.sh)
server or MiniMax's hosted T2A v2 instead of Edge TTS. Set the frontmatter
keys:

```yaml
---
voice: narrator-zh          # backend-specific voice id — see below
tts_provider: voicebox      # or "minimax"; omit (or "edge") for Edge TTS
---
```

| `tts_provider` | `voice:` means | Requirements | Speed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `voicebox` | Voicebox profile name or id | local voicebox-server (`VOICEBOX_URL`, default `127.0.0.1:17493`) | Qwen3-TTS ~7× slower than realtime (MLX) |
| `minimax` | MiniMax `voice_setting.voice_id` (system voice or cloned voice_id) | `MINIMAX_API_KEY`; **voice cloning needs a pay-as-you-go key — Token Plan keys get error 2061** | ~2.5× faster than realtime |
| omitted / `edge` | Edge TTS voice id (e.g. `zh-CN-YunjianNeural`) | none (free Edge endpoint) | ~realtime |

MiniMax cloning flow (verified 2026-10-18): `POST /v1/files/upload`
(`purpose=voice_clone`, wav ≥10 s) → `POST /v1/voice_clone` → use the
returned `voice_id`. **MiniMax deletes a cloned voice unused for 7 days.**
`speech-2.8-turbo` is the default model; inter-sentence pauses use native
`<#x#>` markers instead of Edge's silence concat.

The TTS cache key includes the provider name, so switching
`tts_provider` (or `voice`) re-synthesizes every scene; Edge-sidecar
hashes are unchanged from before this key existed. An unrecognized
`tts_provider` value warns and falls back to Edge TTS.

`tts_provider` survives re-drafts (it is not drafter-owned), but `voice`
is — a re-draft resets it, so re-set both after `video draft`.

**Pre-flight policy (2026-10-18)**: before `video make` synthesizes, a
voicebox article probes the local server (2 s timeout). Server down →
loud warning + MiniMax system voice (`Chinese (Mandarin)_Male_Announcer`
/ `English_expressive_narrator`); MiniMax key missing too → Edge. The
same probe gates the `video-ask` `tts` question: it is offered (with
your cloned profiles as choices, `--tts` to answer) only when the server
answers with at least one profile; otherwise the draft silently defaults
to `minimax-system`.

### `bake.json` — text baked onto scene images (v0.10.5)

When a scene needs large typography — an opening title, a closing quote — the
text is typeset onto the generated image with Pillow at `video make` time,
instead of rendering the scene as a vector card component. The manifest lives
beside the images:

```json
{
  "scenes": {
    "1":  { "style": "title", "text": "长安清晨，宫门马蹄", "subtext": "公元626年7月2日" },
    "26": { "style": "quote", "text": "当规则无法约束野心……", "attribution": "玄武门之变" }
  },
  "palette": { "color": [244,241,234,255], "accent": [181,83,60,255], "scrim": 125 }
}
```

Text lands in the upper two-thirds; the lower third stays quiet for the
caption overlay. The bake spec is part of the image cache key — an edited
title regenerates the image exactly like an edited `visual:` line does.

The thumbnail inherits both keys too (v0.10.3): `video youtube` passes them to
the agent so `thumbnail_prompt` is written in the video's own style preset and
era, and `video thumbnail` appends the verbatim style contract and the setting
line to the prompt in code — so the match holds even for a
`youtube/thumbnail-prompt.txt` written before this existed. A video rendered
as editorial illustration no longer ships a cinematic-35mm thumbnail.

## Renderer families (plan §9)

| renderer     | component              | notes                                                      |
| ------------ | ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `remotion`   | any REGISTRY component | default                                                    |
| `canvas`     | `DoodleScene`          | hand-drawn ink; `bpm` quantizes stroke onsets              |

## Compiler contract

`compileStoryboard(text, projectRoot, {fps?, width?, height?})` →
`{ renderPlan, yaml, write }`:

- deterministic (byte-identical re-compilation of emitted vdsl.yaml),
- `write()` persists `vdsl/vdsl.yaml` — preview/final compile FROM it when
  fresh and fall back to the storyboard loudly when it is corrupt,
- draft mode (`video preview --draft`) overrides fps/width/height (960×540@15)
  without touching the storyboard.

## Branding (`style.brand`, feature 2026-10-05)

Optional `brand` block on `style` — authored in the storyboard directly or
in a project-level `brand.yaml` (render time merge; `brand.yaml` wins).
Schema: `brandSchema` in `packages/vdsl/src/schema.ts`.

| field                | default        | meaning                                                |
| -------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `name`               | —              | channel name, shown in the intro band                  |
| `icon`               | —              | corner watermark image, every scene, whole duration    |
| `corner`             | `bottom-right` | `top-left`/`top-right`/`bottom-left`/`bottom-right`    |
| `size_px`            | `72`           | watermark edge at 1080p, scales with composition width |
| `opacity`            | `0.85`         | watermark opacity                                      |
| `intro.duration_sec` | `15`           | branded-opening window (omit `intro` = no chrome)      |
| `intro.background`   | `aurora`       | `aurora`/`sunset`/`ocean`/`citrus` gradient            |
| `intro.show_name`    | `true`         | render `name` in the intro band                        |

Renderer: `BrandWatermark` + `BrandIntro` in video-components (overlay
family, not REGISTRY scenes); the icon is inlined as a data URL by
`resolveImageSources` like scene images. Audio counterpart:
`audio-config.yaml` `bgm_tracks` (ordered absolute-second windows, 1 s
crossfades, pre-rendered to `assets/audio-assets/bgm/_timeline.wav`).
